newsitem.title: UAE: Four of 10 Italians kidnapped in Yemen freed.
newsitem.headline: Four of 10 Italians kidnapped in Yemen freed.

text.p: Four Italian tourists, who were among 10 Italians kidnapped by tribesmen in two incidents in Yemen, were released by their abductors on Friday, a diplomatic source said.
"The group of four Italians were released this morning (Friday) after negotiations between the government and the tribal leader," the source in the Yemeni capital Sanaa said.
"They are in good health and negotiations are continuing over the other six Italians," the source told Reuters in Dubai by telephone. He gave no further details.
The four had been abducted in an area some 100 km (60 miles) north of Sanaa, on Thursday morning.

Six Italians, including two children aged nine and 10, were kidnapped in the south of the country on Wednesday, the Italian Foreign Ministry said on Thursday. They had been taken to the interior of the country.
The kidnappings were the latest in a series carried out by Yemeni tribesmen in one of the Arab world's poorest countries.

An Italian kidnapped earlier this month was released last Sunday and two others who were abducted in late July were freed after one day. In March, 11 Germans including seven motorcycle tourists were abducted and later freed.

The tribesmen have tried to use hostages -- who have included French and U.S. diplomats and a Saudi ambassador -- as bargaining chips in land and water disputes with the government and foreign oil firms.
